headline: Sensex Crashes 1,100 Points and Nifty Slips Below 22,300 Amid Rising Oil Prices and High US Bond Yields

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Brent crude oil prices surged toward $100 per barrel, raising inflationary concerns
US 10-year Treasury yields hit their highest levels since 2002
Aggressive and sustained selling of Indian stocks by Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs)
Global market cues including rate hike fears and a broader pullback in global equities
whatHappening: The Sensex plunged over 1,100 points while the Nifty 50 fell below the 22,300 mark
Over ₹10 lakh crore in investor wealth was wiped out during the single-day market crash
Indian share benchmarks are on track for their longest weekly losing streak in 25 years
Midcap and smallcap indices are trading in deep red, significantly underperforming the broader market
summary: Indian equity markets witnessed a massive sell-off today, with the Sensex crashing over 1,100 points and Nifty falling below 22,300. The plunge was triggered by rising crude oil prices, multi-decade high US bond yields, and heavy FII selling. Broader markets also suffered, with mid and small-cap stocks facing intense pressure and wiping out trillions in investor wealth.
